generation.name: recursive additive RGB wheel, circular midpoint insertion
rules: Gen 0: red/green/blue at 0°,120°,240° on an HSV rainbow wheel; these are RGB light primaries, not RYB paint primaries.
Gen g>=1: insert an angular midpoint between every pair of adjacent preexisting hues around 360°; new hues are (2k+1)*60 / (2^(g-1)) degrees for k=0..(3*2^(g-1)-1).
Generation hues do not replace earlier colors. A Gen3 color is a fourth-order subdivision, not an established named class in color science.
Each new hue is available at exactly three independently selected display strengths.
generation.photometricCaveat: HSV display channel scaling is a symbolic brightness operation in sRGB; it is not calibrated photometric intensity or physical force strength.

palette.hueWheel: HSV as computational presentation of additive RGB color primaries

mappingTo370.warning: Virtual generation wheel has >370 distinct accumulated hues by Gen7 (384); nearest-address collisions are expected and must never overwrite fixed address definitions.

preserved.historyVsColorGeneration: Independent meanings: Gen0/Gen1 history anchors remain unchanged; hue generation number is a palette refinement level.

limitations: Generation-to-color naming is a configurable computational representation, not an empirical law of matter emergence.
Weak, Medium and Strong refer to symbolic intensity tiers and are not the weak/strong nuclear forces, electromagnetism, or objectively defined intermediate forces.
Red/yellow/blue paint primaries follow a different simplified color-mixing convention; this digital additive RGB overlay is chosen explicitly.
HSV is a nonlinear color model for display; physical spectral mixing is not fully described by hue midpoints.
The 370 indexed source colors and three orbit boundaries are preserved, not retroactively renamed primary/secondary/tertiary.
Virtual hues share approximate addresses once the generational subdivision becomes fine enough; do not treat identical address as identical source or provenance.
